sentences.text: As per the facts of the case on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , the petitioner alongwith her family members were going in a car, from Nazafgarj, to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

And when they reached at main road Deenpur, opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered simple injuries due to this accident.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No. (i): Whether Gun, Annu, Sharda Devi, Ashwani Chaurasia and Asha Ram Chaurasia sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt.
11.03.2014 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle No. DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent No.3 ? OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
Petitioner, herself examined as PW1.
Sh Ashwani Chaurasia as PW2 and Ms Anuu as PW3 10.

PW 1 in her evidence, filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , she alongwith her family members were going in a car from her house to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

She has deposed that when they reached at main road, Deenpur opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered injuries due to this accident.

PW2 and PW3 have deposed on the same lines Annu vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187493403/
6
as deposed by PW.1 11.PW 1 , PW2 and PW3
have been crossexamined, but nothing material could come out in their cross examination which could disbelief their testimony.
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a MACT No. 130/16 Annu vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 8 of 13 matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim's car driver was at fault, in any way.

sentences.text: 12.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by the medical documents ie MLC No.1135/14,annexed with the DAR.
After investigation, police has also indicted respondent no. 1 as an accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 3.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.3 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a car bearing No.DL1LE8126 by respondent no. 3 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ?
Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom? ... OPO 13.
Being injured, petitioner is well within her rights to claim compensation.
It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 3 and the MLC No.1135/14 the petitioner was removed to RTRM Hospital for her treatment.

It is deposed by her that due to the said accident, she herself and her family members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, loss of social activities etc.
14.

So considering all the facts compensation is awarded as under:
MEDICAL EXPENSES 15.
The petitioner has not placed on record medical bills of Rs.856/ MACT No. 130/16 Annu vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 9 of 13
There is no rebuttal to these medical bills Ex PW3/1 ( Colly).
But , seeing the injuries being suffered by petitioner, a lump sum amount of Rs.2,000/ is granted to her towards medical expenses.
. Attendant Charges , Conveyance and Special Diet.

16. As far as attendant charges are concerned petitioner has not led any PE in this regard, yet,
considering the stay of hospitalization of petitioner seeing the nature of injuries being suffered by petitioner , an amount of Rs.2,000/, is being awarded for attendant charges.
Moreover, a sum of Rs. 2,000/ for special diets, Rs.2,000/ for conveyance is also awarded to the petitioner.
Pain and suffering 17.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.

It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the Annu vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187493403/
7 mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.15,000/ is awarded to her.

Mental and physical shock:

OPP (ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?
This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent by holding that accident in question took place due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent no.3 and petitioner suffered injuries in that accident and petitioner is entitled for compensation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
And when they reached at main road Deenpur, opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered simple injuries due to this accident.
2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).
The petitioner has filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 50,00,000/ ( Fifty Lacs ) from respondents as compensation,
alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
3. The respondent No.1 has filed reply/WS stating therein that a false case been filed against him to extort money from him.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the Annu vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187493403/
7 mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
The petitioner was 60 years of age at the time of accident but due to this mishappening with her, all her dreams and expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
with this petition, the IO of the case after verification of insurance policy found it a fake one and charge sheeted the accused/ respondent No.3 for the offence U/S 420/468/471 IPC and U/S 146/196 M.V Act.

23. In the given circumstances, the respondent No.2, insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of offending vehicle.
24. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent No.1 and 3 by holding that petitioner is entitled for compensation from respondent 1 and 3.
ISSUE No. 3 (RELIEF) MACT No. 130/16 Annu vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 12 of 13 25.
Petition in hands is allowed.
Respondent no.1 and 3 are directed to pay Rs.33,000/ with interest @ 7.5% from the date of filing of petition i.e. 12.11.2014 till the date of compliance to the petitioner as compensation in this case, within 30 days from today.
Thereafter interest @ 12% p.a for delayed payment.
Amount of interim compensation (if any) be deducted from this amount.
The awarded amount shall remain as tax free.
26. Considering the facts and circumstances, the entire amount be released to the petitioner alongwith cumulative interest thereon.
27. Respondent no..1 and 3 directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal,
within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
